newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Canadian force leader Baril to east Zaire Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Canadian force leader Baril to east Zaire Thursday.

text.p: The Canadian military leader of the proposed multinational intervention force for eastern Zaire will visit the rebel-held border town of Goma on Thursday, a rebel Zairean source said.
An aide to rebel leader Laurent Kabila said Lieutenant-General Maurice Baril would meet Kabila during his visit. It was not clear whether he would go outside Goma.
Deployment of the mission is bogged down in political indecision, with many countries losing all enthusiasm after up to 600,000 refugees returned home to Rwanda in mid-November.

Western military reconnaissance teams and aid agencies are trying to establish how many refugees are left in eastern Zaire, and exactly where they are. Aid agencies estimated there were 1.2 million there before the recent exodus.

The Zairean rebels reject the multinational force for east Zaire, arguing there are few refugees in areas they control so any international military presence would prop up President Mobutu Sese Seko, currently convalescing in Europe.

Rwanda's government says any aid would be best used within Rwandan territory, providing for the new returnees, but aid agencies say a multinational force is still needed to reach hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees and Zaireans displaced by fighting in eastern Zaire.
